---
title: "MSMS release notes"
---

## Version 2.6.2 (November 2026)

A robustness release: it fixes crashes on large or unusual inputs, merges duplicate atoms instead
of stopping, and runs `-all_components` in parallel. It is available for
[Linux, macOS and Windows](download.qmd). The macOS and Windows packages were added on
November 12, 2026; they give byte-identical output on the regression suite.

**Output is unchanged.** For inputs that 2.6.1 handled, the `.vert`, `.face` and `.area` files
are byte-for-byte identical to those of the 2.6.1 source built with the same compiler. This was
checked on 117 cases of the regression suite, at densities 1 and 3, with and without
`-all_components`. The 2007 2.6.1 binaries were built with a much older compiler. Compared with
them, a few coordinates can differ in the last printed digit and a few triangles can be stitched
differently.

### Crashes fixed

These inputs used to crash, hang or write corrupt files:

- **Very large surfaces.** A component with more than 2 million triangles or vertices overflowed
  the output buffers, which corrupted the files or crashed MSMS.
- **Large molecules.** At around 100,000 atoms the recursive surface construction overflowed the
  default 8 MB stack. MSMS now runs the computation on a thread with a large stack. The traversal
  order, and so the output, is unchanged.
- **Very large and very small spheres.** Radii above about 37 Å (at the default `hdensity` of 3)
  and around 0.4 Å overflowed the triangulation templates.
- **Faces with many points.** Faces with more than 10,000 points overflowed the stitching arrays,
  which are now sized for each face.
- **Many components.** `-all_components` crashed beyond 253 surface components. The limit is now
  65,535.
- **Recovery from numerical problems.** Some paths taken after a degenerate configuration crashed
  or hung instead of restarting with enlarged atoms:
  - "third atom not found" recursed until the stack overflowed;
  - the last retry built the surface on an incomplete reduced surface;
  - the spatial tree was freed twice;
  - merged components were used after being freed;
  - more than 4 singular edges overflowed an array.
- **Exact tangency.** Rounding produced square roots of slightly negative numbers (NaN). These
  are now clamped to 0.
- **Spatial search tree.** It read past the end of an array for some atom distributions.
- **Input.** A field longer than 19 characters in the sphere file, such as a long atom name,
  overflowed a buffer. File names longer than the internal buffers are now rejected with an
  error.

### Duplicate atoms

Two atoms with exactly the same centre used to stop the run with "identical centers". MSMS now:

- keeps one atom per centre: the one with the largest radius, or the first in the file if the
  radii are equal;
- prints a warning for each atom it merges;
- reports atoms closer than 0.001 Å.

Numbering still follows the input file. This applies to the sphere numbers in `.vert` files, the
`.area` rows (a merged atom gets a row with zero area) and the `-one_cavity` atom indices.

### Faster `-all_components`

With `-all_components`, the search for a starting face on buried atoms now runs in parallel
(OpenMP). The output is the same for any number of threads. `OMP_NUM_THREADS` sets the number of
threads; by default MSMS uses all cores.

| Input | 2.6.1 | 2.6.2, 8 threads |
|---|---|---|
| 1gd1 | 0.89 s | 0.47 s |
| pbmol | 2.03 s | 1.03 s |

### Binaries

- **Linux:** `msms.x86_64Linux2.2.6.2.staticgcc` is statically linked and runs on any 64-bit x86
  Linux; `msms.x86_64Linux2.2.6.2` needs glibc 2.34 or later, libtirpc and libgomp.
- **macOS:** `msms.universalDarwin.2.6.2` is one universal binary for Apple silicon (macOS 11 or
  later) and Intel Macs (macOS 10.15 or later).
- **Windows:** `msms.exe` runs on 64-bit Windows, and on Windows on Arm through x64 emulation. It
  needs `libomp.dll`, which is in the same zip file.

## Version 2.6.1

- `find_free_edges` now continues when an atom is completely inside another atom.

## Version 2.6.0

- **Dual density.** A surface can now be computed with 2 vertex densities. The new `-hdensity`
  option gives the density for the high-density region. A flag on each atom marks the
  high-density region. This flag comes before the name field in the input file, so `.xyzrn`
  files are not compatible with earlier versions.
- Edges in cycles made of only 2 edges are now always subdivided.
- If numerical instability stops the reduced surface from building, MSMS can now restart the
  calculation.

## Version 2.5.7

- **Vertex type field fixed.** It is now:
  - 3 for vertices inside reentrant faces;
  - 2 for vertices in toroidal faces and on SES edges and vertices;
  - 1 for vertices inside contact faces.
